title: The Face Taking Shape
logline: A sculptor has spent three weeks on the eyes of a Buddha image and still isn't satisfied. He won't say what he's looking for, only that he'll know it when the face stops looking back.

object.note: Object 6 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From a community holding one member in mind to a sculptor holding one face in mind, in detail, for weeks.

thread_out.thread: The patient attention given to a carved face becomes care given to living ones: a mother's single day moving between children who each need something different.

requirements: A family or workshop currently completing a Buddha image, willing to allow filming over enough time
Access to the maker's own account of his process and beliefs, not assumptions imposed on him
No disruption to a live commission
